blocks.text: Maharṣi Vyāsa, another son of Satyavatī, fathered children with the widows, leading to the birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and Vidura. Adding to the previous irony, both Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu were considered unfit to be the King. And another was born, Vidura, but to a maid. Though he was exemplary, he too could not be the King. Pāṇḍu was chosen and he ruled well, only to die too soon, with heirs not old enough. The throne is left empty yet again.

This throne finds a stable king only at the end of the Kurukṣetra war. Though Yudhiṣṭira becomes king in between, he is unseated by Duryodhana's wicked plots. Now one has to wonder, "Was this pratijñā so important?" How many people may have suffered from this continued kinglessness? In the end, 18 akṣauhiṇīs of soldiers died in battle.
